title: Android 15/16 Samsung FRP Unlock
desc: Uses bleeding-edge AT modem commands in order to attempt to unlock the device and remove FRP.
pros: Works on most Samsung devices on Android 15/16
Will not cause harm upon failure
Most other tools do not have this unlock as of early Jan. 2026
cons: Needs a slightly more powerful PC
Not confirmed to function properly
Bleeding-edge code is less likely to work

title: 2024 FRP Unlock
desc: Attempts to use AT in order to overload and trick the system into enabling ADB, and then using that to unlock the device.
pros: Works on most devices still on the 2024 patch
Similar functionality to older methods
cons: Needs a slightly more powerful PC
Only confirmed to work on U.S. models

title: 2022-2023 FRP Unlock
desc: Attempts to use AT in order to overload and trick the system into enabling ADB, and then using that to unlock the device.
pros: Works on most devices still 2022-2023 patch
Similar functionality to older methods
cons: Not confirmed to work on all devices

title: Pre-2022 FRP Unlock
desc: Attempts to use AT in order to easily enable ADB, and then using that to unlock the device.
pros: Works on most devices still pre-2022 patch
The OG unlock method used by tons of tools
cons: Doesn't work on anything past 2022-patch

title: AT+FRPUNLCK Direct FRP Unlock
desc: Sends the AT+FRPUNLCK command sequence directly to the modem to clear the FRP lock bit without relying on ADB overload tricks.
pros: Faster than overload-based methods
Works on many 2023-2025 Samsung devices
Does not require a specific patch window
cons: Requires MTP mode and a working AT modem connection
Not guaranteed on all firmware versions
Device must accept AT+FRPUNLCK commands

title: CSC Rapid-Switch FRP Bypass
desc: Rapidly cycles through CSC configurations via AT commands to confuse the FRP state machine, then uses ADB to complete the bypass.
pros: Can work on devices resistant to overload methods
Compatible with most Samsung devices on 2022-2025 patches
Low risk of device damage
cons: May change regional settings temporarily
Requires restoring CSC after unlock
Not confirmed on all carrier-locked models

title: AT OEM Unlock Enable
desc: Uses AT debug-level and test-mode commands to set the OEM unlock flag on the device without needing to navigate Developer Options.
pros: Unlocks OEM without enabling Developer Options first
Useful when the UI is completely locked behind FRP
Works independently of the security patch level
cons: Trips Knox warranty bit on most devices
Requires the device to respond to AT+DEBUGLVL commands
Results vary across device models

title: 2025 Modem Overload FRP Unlock
desc: Updated overload sequence targeting 2025 Samsung firmware. Sends an extended burst of AT commands that exploit a timing window in the modem firmware to force-enable ADB.
pros: Targets devices on 2025 security patches
Extended command set increases success rate
Builds on proven 2022-2024 overload techniques
cons: Takes longer than older methods (~15 min)
Not confirmed on all 2025 firmware variants
Requires a fast USB connection

title: AT+FACTORST Selective Reset
desc: Uses the AT+FACTORST command to perform a selective factory reset that clears FRP partition data while minimizing data loss.
pros: Directly targets FRP partition
Can work when other AT methods fail
Selective reset reduces full data wipe risk
cons: Some data may still be cleared
Device must be in MTP+modem mode
Not compatible with all Samsung firmware

title: AT+DELOCK Network/SIM Unlock
desc: Attempts to carrier-unlock the device using AT+DELOCK commands sent directly through the modem. Works on Samsung devices locked to specific carriers.
pros: Can remove carrier SIM lock permanently
No third-party unlock server required
Works on most Samsung modems
cons: Does not remove FRP — separate step needed
Success depends on carrier lock type
May not work on newer One UI devices

title: USBSW Mode-Switch ADB Race
desc: Switches the Samsung device's USB interface mode via AT+USBSW commands to force an ADB re-enumeration, then races ADB commands in before FRP can re-assert.
pros: Works on devices where standard overload fails
Fast method — under 5 minutes
Does not overload modem commands
cons: Timing-sensitive — success varies by PC speed
Only confirmed on select Exynos models
Requires quick reflexes to authorize ADB

title: AT+OMCCODE Carrier Config Reset
desc: Resets the carrier configuration on the device by changing the OMC code via AT commands, which can clear network-level FRP restrictions on carrier-locked devices.
pros: Targets carrier-level FRP restrictions
Works alongside standard FRP unlocks
Non-destructive to user data
cons: Does not fully remove Google FRP alone
Best used as a supplementary step
May change carrier-specific features

title: LG Screen Unlock
desc: Attempts to use AT in order to easily unlock the device.
pros: Works on most devices still pre-G5
cons: Doesn't work on anything past-G5

title: Moto Fastboot FRP Unlock
desc: This unlock method utilizes fastboot in order to attempt to delete partitions which contain FRP lock info.
pros: Likely to unlock on most Motorola devices
Quick method, fast to try
cons: May not be easy for average users
Can be hard to get into fastboot
Not likely to work on more recent devices.
